comparison: Perfect agreement on C1-C10. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the genomic and structural characterization of H. neptunium bactofilins without critique.

Perfect agreement on C11-C21. Both evaluations support the phenotypic characterization of BacA deletion mutants, complementation experiments, and the conclusion about BacA's critical role in morphogenesis.

Strong agreement on C22-C29. Both support the time-lapse microscopy data showing BacA depletion phenotypes and the inference about BacA maintaining the polar growth zone. Peer review R3 also covers C30-C36 from OpenEval R4.

Strong agreement on C30-C36. Both support the HADA pulse-labeling data and the conclusion that bactofilins limit cell wall biosynthesis to growth zones. Peer review R3 groups these claims with C22-C29.
Perfect agreement on C37-C39. Both accept the growth rate measurements and muropeptide analysis showing unchanged global peptidoglycan composition despite morphological defects.

Disagreement on C40-C46. OpenEval finds the co-polymerization evidence supported, but peer reviewers rate it as UNCERTAIN, noting that AlphaFold predictions don't show the co-polymer and in vitro experiments only tested BacA alone. Reviewers suggest weakening the statement or adding more evidence.
Strong agreement on C47-C58. Both support the dynamic localization patterns across the cell cycle. Peer review R6 also covers C59-C65 from OpenEval R8-R9.
Strong agreement on C59-C63. Both support the co-localization data and the hierarchical interaction between BacA and BacD. Peer review R6 groups these with C47-C58 and C64-C65.
Strong agreement on C64-C65. Both support the F130R polymerization mutant data showing that polymerization is essential for BacA function. Peer review R6 groups these with C47-C63.
Strong agreement on C66-C72. Both support the RodZ localization data and the conclusion that bactofilins exclude elongasomes from the stalk. Peer review R7 also covers C73-C76 from OpenEval R11.

Strong agreement on C73-C76. Both support the comparison between wild-type and mutant RodZ localization demonstrating bactofilins' role as a diffusion barrier. Peer review R7 groups these with C66-C72.

Partial disagreement on C77-C87. OpenEval finds the single-molecule tracking data supported, but peer reviewers rate it as UNCERTAIN, requesting additional analysis including individual snapshots, intensity traces, and confinement event analysis to confirm single-molecule detection.

Perfect agreement on C88-C90. Both support the bioinformatic analysis showing genomic co-occurrence of bactofilins and LmdC homologs across 226 species and the inference of conserved functional association.
Strong agreement on C91-C97. Both support the bioinformatic predictions and structural modeling of LmdC. Peer review R10 also covers C98-C101 from OpenEval R15.
Strong agreement on C98-C101. Both support the in vitro peptidoglycan hydrolysis assays demonstrating LmdC's DD-endopeptidase activity. Peer review R10 groups these with C91-C97.
Strong agreement on C102-C105. Both accept the evidence for LmdC essentiality based on inability to delete or conditionally express the gene. Peer review R11 also covers C106-C111 from OpenEval R17.

Strong agreement on C106-C111. Both support the CRISPRi depletion experiments showing similar phenotypes between LmdC depletion and BacA deletion, supporting the same-pathway model. Peer review R11 groups these with C102-C105.

Perfect agreement on C112-C115. Both support the bio-layer interferometry data demonstrating direct interaction between LmdC and BacA with KD ~15 µM, and identification of the N-terminal region as the binding site.
Strong agreement on C116-C120. Both support the genomic and structural characterization of the R. rubrum bactofilin-LmdC module. Peer review R13 also covers C121-C126 from OpenEval R20-R21.

Strong agreement on C121-C124. Both support the R. rubrum mutant phenotypes and quantitative sinuosity measurements showing that BacARs and LmdCRs act in the same pathway. Peer review R13 groups these with C116-C120 and C125-C126.

Strong agreement on C125-C126. Both support the muropeptide analysis showing unchanged global peptidoglycan composition in R. rubrum mutants, paralleling H. neptunium results. Peer review R13 groups these with C116-C124.

Strong agreement on C127-C130. Both support the R. rubrum localization data showing BacARs and LmdCRs co-localize at the inner curve and the inference about promoting cell wall biosynthesis to reduce curvature. Peer review R14 also covers C131-C134 from OpenEval R23.

Strong agreement on C131-C134. Both support the mutual dependence of BacARs and LmdCRs for proper localization, establishing the hierarchical and reciprocal nature of their interaction. Peer review R14 groups these with C127-C130.

Strong agreement on C135-C139. Both support the mutagenesis data showing that the β-hairpin (cluster I) is critical for LmdC-BacA interaction and proper localization. Peer review R15 also covers C140-C141 from OpenEval R25.
Strong agreement on C140-C141. Both accept the differential effects of cluster II mutations and the speculation about residual aberrant interaction. Peer review R15 groups these with C135-C139.

Perfect agreement on C142. Both strongly support the overarching conclusion about a conserved bactofilin-hydrolase module governing bacterial morphogenesis, based on the combined evidence from H. neptunium and R. rubrum studies.
